options: The surface of a flat shape
questions.explanation: Volume is how much space a solid takes up.
questions.misconception: Surface is area and the outline is perimeter — volume is specifically the space INSIDE a 3D object.

questions.explanation: We count unit CUBES packing the solid, so volume uses cubic units.
questions.misconception: Square units measure flat area and plain units measure length — the solid's three dimensions call for cubic units.

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a box 5 long, 3 wide, and 2 tall?
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubic units.
questions.misconception: All three dimensions multiply together — 5 × 3 = 15 only gets the base layer, missing the height.

questions.prompt: A box's base layer holds 12 cubes and it is 3 layers tall. Its volume is...
questions.explanation: Base area × height layers: 12 × 3 = 36 cubic units.
questions.misconception: Volume stacks the base layer for every layer of height — the base alone is only one layer.

options: How much water fits in the pool
How much fence around the yard
How much carpet for the floor
How many tiles on the wall
questions.explanation: Water filling a pool measures its interior space — volume.
questions.misconception: Fence is perimeter, carpet is area, and tiles cover a surface — only filling a 3D space needs volume.
